findings.text: Crypto header defines a single include guard macro to prevent multiple inclusion.

Filesystem cache cookie lifecycle helpers expose unuse, relinquish, update, resize and invalidate operations. Each wrapper first checks a cookie state predicate for validity or enablement and only then delegates to an internal helper; otherwise it does nothing. Unuse accepts auxiliary data and size observations, relinquish accepts a retirement flag, update accepts auxiliary data and size, resize accepts a new length, and invalidate accepts auxiliary data with size and flags.

Auxiliary cache metadata is stored either inline or externally depending on its length relative to inline capacity. Retrieval selects the appropriate backing. Update copies caller supplied bytes only when both source and destination exist and refreshes the recorded object size only when a size pointer is supplied.

Marking a cookie for update follows a fixed order: account for the update when statistics are enabled, refresh auxiliary and size information, enforce ordering against later flag observation, then set the needs-update indicator. The enabled-state wrapper ensures this sequence runs only for enabled cookies.

Cache I/O sessions are opened through read and write begin helpers that return a no-buffer indication when the cookie is not enabled and otherwise delegate to internal begin routines. A validity helper derives an operation table pointer from resource state, yielding null when resources are invalid. Session teardown invokes the table end hook only when the table is present.

Read and write dispatch retrieve the operation table from resources and immediately invoke the corresponding method without checking for absence, unlike session teardown which guards. Callers must therefore guarantee that resources passed to read and write are valid; otherwise a null table dereference occurs. Read additionally carries start offset, iterator, hole handling, and completion callback context; write carries start, iterator and completion context.

Page bookkeeping helpers are gated by a caching flag. Clearing of page state does nothing when caching is false and delegates otherwise. Cache write reports no-buffer completion through the caller callback when caching is false and delegates with full mapping, range, size and callback context when true. Missing callbacks are tolerated in the non-caching path.

Page release observes cookie flags and nullness. When the cookie exists and both the have-data and no-data-to-read indicators are present, it clears the latter to force future reads to consult the cache. In all other states it leaves flags unchanged.

Filename handling uses a byte buffer descriptor pairing an unsigned byte pointer with a 32-bit length, and a larger name record holding the user filename reference, a disk name descriptor, two 32-bit hash values, a crypto scratch descriptor, and a nokey boolean.
File contents encryption alignment requirement is 16 bytes.
Maximum accepted context size for setting encryption context is 40 bytes.
Maximum number of block devices reportable for encrypted contents is 8.

Filesystem crypto integration is described by a table holding an inode info offset, four single-bit capability indicators for block orientation, bounce pooling, narrow inode support and small data units, a legacy key prefix string, and callbacks for retrieving and installing contexts, fetching dummy policy, testing directory emptiness and inode stability, and enumerating content devices within the stated device limit. Context installation is bounded by the stated max size and runs under write-held inode semaphore; emptiness check also runs under write-held semaphore; stability check defaults to false when absent.
Three helpers expose filename views: one builds a counted string view from a buffer descriptor, and two project the disk name pointer and length from a name record.

Enabled builds provide a raw per-inode crypto info accessor that dereferences filesystem specific storage and warns when absent, and a content encryption need predicate that is true only for encrypted regular files.

Dentry crypto marking serializes flag mutation with the dentry lock. Setting the nokey indicator always takes the lock. Clearing the revalidate optimization takes the lock only after observing both the revalidate flag and the expected revalidate handler, tolerating a benign race that at worst costs an extra revalidation. Nokey testing reads the flag without locking.

Enabled builds treat a null address space association as the bounce marker for pages and folios. Translation from bounce to page cache follows private storage. These helpers allow filesystems to distinguish temporary encryption buffers from page cache entries.
Enabled dummy policy state is a wrapper holding a policy union pointer. Presence is tested by null comparison. Release frees the pointed-to policy and nulls the holder.
Enabled builds release filename crypto scratch storage and install the filesystem crypto operation table onto the superblock.
When crypto support is disabled, content encryption need, nokey name, and bounce page and folio predicates are constant false, and dentry preparation is a no-op ignoring its inputs.

Disabled builds fail block oriented encryption with a not-supported indication and fail bounce to page cache translation with a warning plus invalid-argument error pointer. Bounce page release is a silent no-op. Directory entry hashing warns and yields zero.

Disabled builds reject policy and nonce ioctls and context installation with not-supported, reject dummy encryption parsing with invalid-argument, permit context inheritance checks, treat any two dummy policies as equal, and make dummy display, dummy release and dummy presence test no-ops with presence always false. The disabled dummy policy record carries no fields.
Disabled builds reject all keyring ioctls for adding, removing, removing for all users, and querying key status with a not-supported indication.

Disabled builds allow new inode preparation and file open only when the relevant directory or inode is unencrypted and otherwise reject with not-supported; link, rename, lookup, partial lookup, readdir and setattr preparation always reject with not-supported, while encryption info release and inode free are silent no-ops and inode drop always reports keep.

Disabled filename setup passes through the input name after zeroing the output record when the directory is unencrypted and rejects with not-supported when encrypted; freeing and buffer release are no-ops while buffer allocation rejects with not-supported. Name matching uses length plus byte comparison, directory revalidation always reports valid, symlink preparation passes through short targets with length check and rejects encrypted directories or overlong targets, while symlink encryption, symlink content retrieval and symlink attribute query reject with not-supported and superblock operation installation is a no-op.
